title: Four Sights and the Great Going Forth
bigQuestion: How do Buddhist texts tell the story of the Buddha's early life, and which parts come from which texts?

story.title: One Last Look
story.kicker: At midnight a prince looks once at his sleeping baby son and then rides away.
paragraphs: Buddhist life stories tell this scene. It is midnight in the palace at Kapilavastu. Music has stopped. The dancers are asleep on the floor. Prince Siddhartha is awake.
He walks quietly to the room where his wife, Yasodhara, is sleeping. Their newborn son, Rahula, lies beside her. Her hand rests on the baby's head. The prince stands in the doorway.
The story says he wants to hold his son one time. But if he moves her hand, she will wake. If she wakes, he may not be able to leave. So he only looks. Then he turns away.
In the courtyard, his driver Channa waits with the white horse Kanthaka. The prince climbs on. The story says the gods muffle the horse's hooves so no one hears. The city gate swings open by itself.
By morning he is far from home. At a river he cuts off his long hair with his sword. He trades his fine clothes for a simple robe. Buddhists call this night the Great Going Forth.
story.think: Why do you think this scene has been painted and retold so many times?

lessons.title: Queen Maya's Dream
lessons.mainIdea: Buddhist tradition says Queen Maya dreamed of a white elephant before Siddhartha was born.
reading: Buddhist life stories begin with a dream. Queen Maya, wife of King Suddhodana, dreamed that a white elephant came to her. It carried a white lotus flower. Wise men said she would have a great son.

The king and queen ruled the Sakya people. Their city was Kapilavastu, near today's border of India and Nepal. The family name was Gotama. That is why Buddhists also call the Buddha "Gotama" or "Gautama."
In many parts of Asia, a white elephant is a sign of honor and good luck. Temple paintings often show Maya's dream. It is one of the first scenes in many picture stories of the Buddha's life.

words.d: the clan, or large family group, the Buddha was born into
the Sakya capital city where tradition says Siddhartha grew up

look.title: A Painted Dream
look.text: A temple wall shows a queen asleep on a couch. Above her floats a small white elephant with six tusks. It holds a lotus in its trunk. Gold light surrounds it.
look.prompt: What do the white color and the lotus suggest about the baby to come?

check.q: What did Queen Maya dream about, says tradition?
check.why: Buddhist life stories say Maya dreamed of a white elephant.

check.q: Who was Siddhartha's father?
check.why: Tradition names King Suddhodana of the Sakyas as his father.

check.q: Why do Buddhists also call the Buddha "Gotama"?
check.why: Gotama (Sanskrit Gautama) was the family name.

lessons.title: Born in Lumbini
lessons.mainIdea: Tradition says Siddhartha was born in a garden at Lumbini, a place Buddhists visit today.
reading: The stories say Queen Maya was traveling to her parents' home to give birth. She stopped in a garden called *Lumbini*. There, holding the branch of a tree, she gave birth to a son.

Later stories add wonders. They say the baby took seven steps, and lotus flowers bloomed under his feet. Buddhists in many lands celebrate his birthday. Many pour sweet tea or water over a small statue of the baby Buddha.
Lumbini is in Nepal today. In about 249 BCE, King Ashoka set up a stone pillar there. Its writing says the Buddha was born at that place. Pilgrims still visit the garden.

words.d: the garden in today's Nepal where tradition says the Buddha was born
a person who travels to a holy place

look.title: Dating the Buddha
look.cite: Theravada tradition; scholarly estimates summarized in Gethin, The Foundations of Buddhism (1998)
look.prompt: Why might dates for the Buddha's birth differ by over 100 years?

check.q: Where does tradition say the Buddha was born?
check.why: Tradition and Ashoka's pillar name Lumbini, in today's Nepal.

check.q: What did King Ashoka put at Lumbini?
check.why: Ashoka's pillar there says the Buddha was born at that place.

check.q: What is a pilgrim?
choices: a person who travels to a holy place
check.why: A pilgrim travels to a holy place.

lessons.title: Old Texts and Later Stories
lessons.mainIdea: The oldest suttas say little about the Buddha's childhood; fuller life stories came later.
reading: Many details you know come from later books. The oldest suttas mostly record the Buddha's teachings. They mention his early life only in short bits. For example, one sutta has him recall a calm moment as a boy under a rose-apple tree.

Full life stories came later. The *Buddhacarita*, "Acts of the Buddha," is a long Sanskrit poem. Tradition names its author Ashvaghosha. Scholars date it to about the 1st or 2nd century CE. The Pali commentary on the Jatakas also tells the whole story.
Scholars compare these texts to see how the story grew. Buddhists read them as honored accounts of the Buddha's life. Both kinds of readers find meaning in the details.

words.d: "Acts of the Buddha," a long Sanskrit poem about his life by Ashvaghosha
the story of a person's life

look.title: A Memory Under a Tree
look.text: The Buddha recalls a day in his childhood. His father was working in the fields. He sat in the cool shade of a rose-apple tree, and his mind grew quiet and happy.
look.prompt: How is this short memory different from the long palace stories?

check.q: What is the Buddhacarita?
choices: a Sanskrit poem about the Buddha's life
check.why: The Buddhacarita is Ashvaghosha's poem, "Acts of the Buddha."

check.q: Which texts say little about the Buddha's childhood?
check.why: The oldest suttas mostly record teachings, with only short bits about his youth.

check.q: About when do scholars date the Buddhacarita?
check.why: Scholars date Ashvaghosha to about the 1st or 2nd century CE.

sections.title: The Four Sights and Leaving Home

lessons.title: Four Sights
lessons.mainIdea: Life stories say an old man, a sick man, a dead man and a wandering holy man led Siddhartha to leave home.
reading: The life stories say King Suddhodana kept his son in comfort. A wise man had predicted the boy would become a great king or a great teacher. The king wanted a king. So he kept sad sights away.
On trips outside the palace, the prince saw four things. He saw an old man, a sick man and a dead body. Then he saw a calm wandering holy man. Buddhists call these the *Four Sights*.

An older sutta tells this same story, but about an earlier Buddha named Vipassi (Digha Nikaya 14). Later biographies tell it about Siddhartha. Buddhists read the Four Sights as showing the problems every person faces.

words.d: an old man, a sick man, a dead man and a holy man, which led Siddhartha to leave home
a person who gives up comforts to seek spiritual truth

look.title: Two Tellings
look.text: In Digha Nikaya 14, the Four Sights happen to a Buddha of long ago named Vipassi. In the Buddhacarita, they happen to Siddhartha. The sights and lessons are almost the same.
look.prompt: Why might Buddhist teachers tell the same pattern about more than one Buddha?

check.q: Which is one of the Four Sights?
check.why: The Four Sights are an old man, a sick man, a dead man and a holy man.

check.q: Which sutta tells the Four Sights about Vipassi?
check.why: Digha Nikaya 14 tells the pattern about the earlier Buddha Vipassi.

check.q: Why did the king hide sad sights, say the stories?
choices: he wanted his son to become a king
check.why: A wise man predicted a great king or a great teacher, and the king wanted a king.

lessons.title: The Great Going Forth
lessons.mainIdea: Tradition says Siddhartha left home at night on his horse Kanthaka to seek an answer to suffering.
reading: Siddhartha was 29, the stories say. He had a wife, Yasodhara, and a baby son, Rahula. One night he left with his driver Channa and his horse *Kanthaka*. Buddhists call this the Great Going Forth.
An older sutta tells it more simply. In Majjhima Nikaya 26, the Buddha says he shaved his head and put on a robe while his parents wept. There is no secret midnight ride in that telling.
Buddhists honor the going forth as a great sacrifice. Some readers today also think about Yasodhara, left behind. Later texts tell that she and Rahula both joined the Buddha's community of followers.

words.d: the white horse Siddhartha rode when he left home, in the life stories
Siddhartha's wife and the mother of Rahula

look.title: An Older Telling
look.text: While I was still young, with black hair, and my mother and father were weeping, I shaved my head and beard, put on the yellow robe, and went forth from home into homelessness.
look.prompt: How is this telling different from the midnight ride?

check.q: What was the name of Siddhartha's horse?
check.why: Kanthaka was the horse; Channa was the driver.

check.q: Who was Rahula?
check.why: Rahula was the son of Siddhartha and Yasodhara.

check.q: In Majjhima Nikaya 26, what were his parents doing when he left?
check.why: In that older sutta he says his parents wept as he went forth.

lessons.title: Teachers and Fasting
lessons.mainIdea: The texts say Siddhartha studied with teachers and then tried hard fasting for years before finding it did not work.
reading: The suttas say Siddhartha first studied with two teachers of meditation. They were Alara Kalama and Uddaka Ramaputta. He learned all they taught. But he felt it did not end suffering.

Next he joined five other ascetics. For about six years he tried hard practices. He fasted until, one sutta says, he could feel his backbone through his stomach. Statues from Gandhara show him very thin.
At last he decided hard fasting did not lead to wisdom. He ate food again, and the stories say Sujata offered him rice cooked in milk. The five companions thought he had given up. They left him.

words.d: an ancient region in today's Pakistan and Afghanistan known for Buddhist statues

look.title: The Fasting Buddha
look.text: A famous stone statue from Gandhara, now in a museum in Lahore, Pakistan, shows Siddhartha seated and very thin. His ribs and veins show. His face is still calm.
look.prompt: What might an artist want viewers to feel when they see this statue?

check.q: Who were two of Siddhartha's first teachers?
check.why: The suttas name Alara Kalama and Uddaka Ramaputta.

check.q: About how long did he practice hard fasting, say the texts?
check.why: Tradition says he spent about six years in hard practices.

check.q: Why did the five companions leave him?
choices: they thought he had given up
check.why: When he ate again, they thought he had given up his search.

lessons.title: The Middle Way
lessons.mainIdea: Buddhists say Siddhartha found a middle way between too much comfort and too much hardship.
reading: Siddhartha had lived in two ways. In the palace he had every comfort. As an ascetic he had almost nothing. The texts say neither one brought the answer he wanted.
Buddhists call the path between them the *middle way*. It is not a lazy path. It asks for steady effort, like tuning a string not too tight and not too loose.
The Buddha later began his first sermon by naming two extremes to avoid. One is chasing pleasure. The other is harming yourself. Between them, he said, is the middle way.

words.d: the path between too much comfort and too much hardship
going too far in one direction

look.title: Two Extremes
look.text: There are two extremes that one who has left home should not follow: chasing sense pleasures, and harming oneself with hard practices. Avoiding both, the Tathagata found the middle way.
look.cite: Samyutta Nikaya 56.11 (the first sermon), paraphrased from T.W. Rhys Davids, Buddhist Suttas, SBE 11 (1881)
look.prompt: What two extremes does this passage name?

check.q: What is the middle way?
choices: the path between too much comfort and too much hardship
check.why: Buddhists describe the middle way as avoiding both extremes.

check.q: Which two extremes does the first sermon name?
check.why: Samyutta Nikaya 56.11 names these two extremes.

check.q: What is an extreme?
choices: going too far in one direction
check.why: An extreme goes too far one way.

lessons.title: Awakening at Bodh Gaya
lessons.mainIdea: Buddhists believe Siddhartha awakened under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya and became the Buddha.
reading: Siddhartha sat beneath a fig tree near the town now called Bodh Gaya. The stories say he vowed not to rise until he understood. A tempter named Mara sent fear and desire to stop him.

Many images show him touching the earth with his right hand. The stories say he called the earth to witness his many good lives. Mara's armies fled. Buddhists believe that, that night, he reached *awakening*.
From then on he was the Buddha, "the awakened one." The tree became the Bodhi tree. Many scholars place these events in the 5th century BCE, but dates vary.

words.d: in Buddhism, seeing the truth about life fully; also called enlightenment
a tempter in Buddhist stories who tried to stop Siddhartha

look.title: The Earth-Touching Pose
look.text: In many Buddha images, he sits cross-legged. His left hand rests in his lap. His right hand reaches down to touch the ground. Buddhists call this the earth-touching gesture.
look.prompt: What part of the story does this pose remember?

check.q: Who tried to stop Siddhartha under the tree, say the stories?
check.why: Buddhist stories name Mara as the tempter.

check.q: What does the earth-touching gesture remember?
check.why: The stories say he touched the earth to call it as witness.

check.q: Where do Buddhists believe he awakened?
check.why: Tradition places the awakening under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya.

review.q: Where does tradition say the Buddha was born?
review.why: Tradition, backed by Ashoka's pillar, names Lumbini.

review.q: Which of these is NOT one of the Four Sights?
review.why: The white elephant was in Maya's dream, not the Four Sights.

review.q: Who wrote the Buddhacarita, says tradition?
review.why: Tradition names Ashvaghosha as its author.

review.q: What is the Great Going Forth?
choices: Siddhartha leaving home to seek truth
review.why: The Great Going Forth is his leaving home.

review.q: How does Majjhima Nikaya 26 differ from the midnight story?
choices: his parents weep as he leaves
he leaves as an old man
review.why: In that older sutta he goes forth openly while his parents weep.

review.q: What did Siddhartha decide about hard fasting?
choices: it did not lead to wisdom
review.why: The texts say he found fasting did not bring the answer.

review.q: What is the Pali name of the first sermon's text?
review.why: The first sermon is Samyutta Nikaya 56.11.

review.q: What do scholars and tradition disagree on?
choices: exact dates of the Buddha's life
review.why: Dates for the Buddha vary by over a century between tradition and scholars.
